issue.description:
ADR-005 records as a drawback that there is no way to mark an assignment as intentionally held, so an operator who deliberately parks work under an assignee gets the doctor warning on every run and learns to ignore it, degrading the warning for everyone. Work needed: design a first-class flag marking an assignment as a deliberate reservation, document its semantics in the native field guide via `bead schema explain`, exclude flagged issues from the ADR-005 ready_frontier warning, round-trip the flag through checkpoint export/restore, and cover it in doctor and list/show output tests.

issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted) commits bead-rs to a third dependency kind `verifies` so inverted verification gates (a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its blocked bead) are diagnosed structurally rather than by title heuristics, deferring it to post-0.1 item R025 — now due at 0.2.x. No open bead covers it. Work: extend the dependency model and section 3.4 validation to accept `verifies` alongside `blocks` without changing the two-kind 0.1 wire contract silently; carry the new edge kind through checkpoint publish/restore round trips and the unknown-field corpus levels; report the inversion diagnosis as an advisory finding (doctor or list output) — report only, never reject the edge at insert time, and never infer the relationship from issue titles; add conformance and concurrency tests per the engineering rules.

issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted) specifies a third dependency kind `verifies` so authors can declare the check relationship, and a structural diagnosis of inverted verification gates (a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its blocked bead). No open bead covers it. Implement the edge kind with atomic, concurrency-tested insertion alongside other dependency mutations and checkpoint round-trip coverage; report the diagnosis (with sample ids and rationale) as advisory only — never reject the edge at insert time, never infer the relationship from issue titles, and leave §3.4 cycle rejection and deliberate 'prove baseline green' gates untouched. Add tests locking in: declared inversion is detected, a deliberate gate is accepted silently, no title heuristics exist anywhere in the path, and the new kind survives export/import. Reference: docs/adr/001-declared-verification-edges-over-title-heuristics.md.
